lines.say: This week, officials said an Israeli strike on a Gaza hospital killed at least six people, despite a ceasefire.
But in 1993, Israelis and Palestinians shook hands on a deal that promised peace.
In September 1993, on the White House lawn, Israel's Yitzhak Rabin and the PLO's Yasser Arafat shook hands.
The Oslo Accords promised Palestinian self-government, and a path to a final peace deal.
A year later, Rabin, Arafat and Shimon Peres shared the Nobel Peace Prize.
In 1995, a second agreement extended Palestinian self-rule. But in November, an Israeli extremist assassinated Rabin.
In 2005, Israel pulled its settlers and soldiers out of Gaza.
Two years later, Hamas took control of the Strip.
Now another ceasefire is under strain.
Can a ceasefire last without a real peace deal?
